metadata.title: Northern Lights on Civic and Citizenship Education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The chapter uses ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016 Nordic-country data and relies on IEA’s IDB Analyzer for weighted descriptive and inferential statistics. For the principal survey analyses, the base weight is defined as the inverse of the school’s selection probability (school size) and is adjusted for non-response to form the final school weight (TOTWGTC). For student- and teacher-level analyses in other chapters referenced in the text, the authors apply student and teacher weights and compute standard errors using jackknife repeated replication (JRR) where applicable. The weighting approach is therefore consistent with ICCS’s two-stage cluster sampling design (schools selected with PPS, then students/teachers sampled within schools), and the manuscript does not indicate any deliberate omission of weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses are based on ICCS 2016 Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden) and focus on grade 8 (grade 9 in Norway/Malta per ICCS design; Norway’s ICCS 2009 grade 9 sample is used in this volume). For the principal-aims chapter, the analytic sample is principals who completed the school-principal questionnaire in ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016, and results are computed using the total school weight (TOTWGTC). For student-scale chapters, the analytic sample uses the available ICCS student survey respondents with IEA’s sampling design and applies student weights; missing data are handled using Mplus full information maximum likelihood (FIML) with treatment of missingness and all five plausible values for cognitive outcomes.

data.outcome_summary: This volume chapter set uses IEA’s ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016 data to examine Nordic patterns in civic and citizenship education, including (i) principals’ prioritized aims for civic and citizenship education, (ii) how open classroom climate and in-school civic participation relate to civic knowledge, citizenship self-efficacy, and intended future electoral participation, and (iii) how home SES, gender, and migrant background relate to an environmental citizenship composite score. The analyses apply ICCS’s two-stage cluster sampling logic and use IEA IDB Analyzer with sampling weights (school weight TOTWGTC for principal responses; student weights for student scales). For cognitive outcomes, the study uses five plausible values and estimates models in Mplus with sampling weights and missing-data treatment via full information maximum likelihood. Reported results show consistent SES gradients in civic competence and evidence that participatory civic learning opportunities are positively associated with civic outcomes, while environmental citizenship is also patterned by SES and gender. Limitations include cross-sectional design (caution on causality) and self-report measures for some constructs.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
